output.summary: KEP-598 proposed adding CRD version conversion via a conversion webhook that the API server calls, with per-version schema, subresources, and printer columns in the CRD spec. The KEP is recorded as implemented at stable stage (status fact: implemented from 2020-12-30).
output.rationale: Version conversion was the most requested CRD improvement, and users needed to evolve APIs without breaking existing clients. The design avoided defaulting per-version fields to top-level fields because that would break backward compatibility, and it instead made a webhook host perform conversion. The sources record the feature's progress through several release cycles, but they do not explain the exact reasoning for the 2020-12-30 implemented status.

alternatives.option: Defaulting per-version fields to top-level spec fields
alternatives.why_not: Per the design, "the defaulting either implicit or explicit has the potential to break backward compatibility as we have two sets of fields representing the same feature."
The design says it "would work but the proposed solution is keeping the mutual excusivity in a broader sense and is preferred."

alternatives.option: Per-version override (per-version X overrides top-level X)
alternatives.why_not: The design says the overriding behaviour "need to be kept in CRD v1 and that looks too complicated and not clean to keep for a v1 API."

evidence.quote: The API Server is extended to call out to a webhook at appropriate parts of the handler stack for CRDs.
Hence the defaulting either implicit or explicit has the potential to break backward compatibility as we have two sets of fields representing the same feature.
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2598 is the PR that moved this KEP to implemented.
The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
